correctness.rationale: Every allowed directed edge or loop is an exposed vertex. Direct joint endpoint moments yield the covariance as two equal diagonal and offdiagonal blocks. Orthogonal symmetric/antisymmetric splitting gives L/N and (D+B)/N-2ww^T/N^2; all four positive eigenvalue formulas follow on an exhaustive clique/independent/group contrast basis, with two null directions. The largest mode is n/N; the least changes sign exactly with H_p(q). The concave polynomial H, its discriminant, and endpoint values at 2,3,4,5 prove all parameter ranges and ties. A Python standard-library checker replayed from the candidate package separately builds 85 exact vertex covariance matrices and verifies their full eigenbases without floating-point arithmetic. No result is extrapolated from finite checks alone.

originality.rationale: The closest full primary source on the identical split-graph PQ polytope, arXiv:2103.15045 Section 4, derives normalized volumes and h-star data rather than uniformly sampled vertex-covariance spectra. The earlier source arXiv:2007.11051 and follow-up arXiv:2202.09853 likewise address enumerative volume questions. Standard complete-split graph Laplacian spectra yield only one of the two covariance blocks after a new moment calculation; they do not imply the centered symmetric eigenspace crossing. Searches of scientific literature and published finding titles/summaries uncovered no equal or dominating covariance theorem. Historical priority is not independently proven.

value.rationale: The PQ adjacency polytope is a studied power-flow-related lattice polytope; the precise covariance spectrum of its distinct vertices is a canonical geometric invariant, not a dimension or vertex-count restatement. The theorem shows two reentrant least-variance eigenspace changes and exact integer cutoffs, including a quadratic scale and a rare double-degeneracy locus. Such orientation shifts are not encoded by existing normalized-volume results and motivate principal-component and geometric sampling comparisons. No downstream theorem or independent historical priority is claimed.
